subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should an explicit managed-service disable for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override persisted state-dir `.env` or config service-env values, or should those persisted sources remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain private prompts and tool output, so automation should not choose the precedence between operator disable intent and durable service env without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat unset, `0`, `off`, and `false` disable intent as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

options.title: Persisted Env Remains Authoritative
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config service env as the durable source, and document that operators must remove those values before restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor-Guided Repair Only
options.body: Leave runtime precedence mostly unchanged but add status/doctor checks that warn and repair stale raw-stream service-env values before operators believe logging is off.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat unset, `0`, `off`, and `false` disable intent as authoritative for managed services, clear or override stale generated service-env entries, and document the precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across raw-stream runtime, durable service env helpers, and merged service-env decisions.
